summary: `auth login`/`auth status`/`auth logout` now prefer the OS keyring (macOS Keychain, Linux Secret Service via D-Bus, Windows Credential Manager) for the access token, refresh token, and confidential-client secret, falling back to the existing 0600 credentials.toml when no keyring backend is available. New file internal/cliutil/keyring.go (best-effort Set/Get/Delete wrapping github.com/zalando/go-keyring); internal/config/config.go's SaveTokens/Load/ClearTokens/saveCredentialsFirst gained a Config.TokenStorage field ("keyring"|"file", never persisted) and the keyring wiring.
reason: Reimplementing the login command against Stytch's own reference (https://stytch.com/docs/connected-apps/guides/cli-agents and https://github.com/stytchauth/stytch-connected-apps-cli-example) surfaced one substantive gap versus the already-correct PKCE/discovery/state-CSRF flow recorded in stytch-connected-apps-login.json: the guide's example stores tokens in the OS keyring specifically for security, not a file. Replacing the file store outright was rejected — this CLI's core design goal is headless/agent/container use (DEUTERO_HOME relocation, sandboxes, doctor --fail-on warn), where OS keyrings are frequently unavailable (no D-Bus secret-service session on a server, no Keychain in CI). Keyring-first-with-file-fallback was chosen after confirming with the user, and after live-reproducing a 'keychain cannot be found to store the credential' failure class in this same session, which is exactly the case the fallback exists for.
validated_outcome: go build/vet/test clean; CGO_ENABLED=0 cross-compiled for the four release targets (darwin/arm64, linux/amd64, linux/arm64, windows/amd64) with go-keyring linked in — all pure Go, no cgo. Unit tests in internal/cliutil/keyring_test.go and internal/config/keyring_test.go cover both the keyring-available and keyring-unavailable (mocked 'keychain cannot be found' error) paths, verifying credentials.toml excludes the secrets when the keyring holds them, a fresh Load() reconstructs AuthHeader() from the keyring, and ClearTokens() removes the keyring entry. Additionally ran a full live end-to-end login against a local mock OIDC/token server on this machine: real macOS Keychain accepted the write, credentials.toml held only client_id + token_expiry, `auth status` reported token_storage=keyring, and `auth logout` removed the real Keychain entry (verified via `security find-generic-password`).
notes: Backward compatible: profiles that logged in before this patch keep their tokens in credentials.toml (LoadKeyringTokens finds nothing there and is a silent no-op); the next `auth login` migrates them to the keyring if one is available. Agentcookie-managed configs are explicitly excluded from the keyring path (SaveTokens/ClearTokens both check AgentcookieManagedByExternalStore() first) since that integration already owns an external secret store. `auth status` and the login success message now report which backend holds the tokens (`token_storage`: "keyring"|"file").
